notes.title: meet Jupiter 🌟 [DEVLOG]
notes.content: [p]Hey cyberware slingers,[/p][p] [/p][p]Today, we’re taking a peek behind the curtain to learn a bit about a yet un-demo-ed character: Jupiter! (Warning for mild spoilers.)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45225636/6ad66154403048c2da613432293bd3d22dd55e4f.png"][/img][/p][p]This scamp is the youngest character in the game and is part of a youth subculture, dubbed Glamscum. Jupiter is 21, is studying at a local university, and uses he/him pronouns.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Likes[/b]: friendship, graffiti, bugs[/p][p][b]Dislikes[/b]: the capitalist machine that runs society, other’s assumptions, being told how to live his life[/p][p][b]Desired mods[/b]: either an animated tattoo, floating hair, or pointed ears (he’s not sure which he’d like)[/p][p] [/p][p]Jupiter was one of the characters we designed quickly, realized we needed to tweak, and then left hanging for months. We recently completed his design, so to celebrate, here’s the full walkthrough of his creation.[/p][p] [/p][p]First, we started with the concept for Jupiter’s character. We knew we wanted a younger client and that we wanted to explore aesthetic mods that were important to both outward and internal identity. Smash these together and add that he has a tight budget since he’s in school, and voila! We now had a character who would be interesting to learn about. (Plus there’s the graffiti, the fact he works part time at the City’s import docks, his hopes and dreams for the future… There’s a lot to ask him about!)[/p][p] [/p][p]Some core elements of Jupiter were his idealism, kindness, and naivete. We wanted to make sure that we reflected these in his design.[/p][p] [/p][p]As with most of our characters in[i] Quality Dreams, Reasonably Priced[/i], we started with designing his outfit. It helps us flesh out the personality more, as we consider how a character might dress, what they prioritize in their styling, and how we can use the outfit to express their personality.[/p][p] [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45225636/c19eb5a92b3898685758e16509fad64e042c0d60.png"][/img][/p][p]We settled on the second outfit with a mix of elements from a few others. The outfit felt free and full of energy. It also lacked some of the try-hard or sporty vibes of the other options, which we decided didn’t fit the character as well.[/p][p] [/p][p]Next, Nez sketched out variations to help us settle on Jupiter’s hair and posture.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45225636/563a8362cee2ddbb3f4ad89e0d0f6058379e1f64.png"][/img][/p][p]From there, we moved to fully rendered sketches of both the character’s poses (with some tweaks along the way).[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45225636/58fa6cc334e6f3568d817ad803a0582cfffe0418.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45225636/1f6de60e3eb42959d5833e40a8db178e507dbf89.png"][/img][/p][p]Then, I finished writing his scene, and we realized that Jupiter needed to be a lot less clean-cut and a lot more punk. (This is where we ended up pausing work on him for quite some time.)[/p][p] [/p][p]More recently, Nez returned to the character and sketched proposed outfit changes on top of the current design.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45225636/d7e395e8ffd07824ca1d2a684913fa23b07db24f.png"][/img][/p][p]Which, after some tweaking...[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45225636/be03201c2307b7eb8f9a10e9304ed636ec34104f.png"][/img][/p][p]...became Jupiter’s new final design! (As seen above.)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45225636/6ad66154403048c2da613432293bd3d22dd55e4f.png"][/img]Almost all of our characters have changed a bit during the writing process, but Jupiter is the only one who’s changed drastically enough to need a redesign. His original design was still something he could wear (especially if trying to clean up for an important appointment), but we felt like it didn’t meld well with his core values.[/p][p] [/p][p]Jupiter desperately wants to be authentic and not to let others dictate his identity. We wanted this to reflect more clearly in his clothes, so we needed to move a bit further away from the good-boy vibes of his first outfit. The vibes are still there (as you can probably see haha), but now they’re presented in a different flavour.[/p][p] [/p][p]Jupiter is a delightful character to write. He brims with enthusiasm, passion, and optimism. We hope that you love him as much as we do![/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]As always, thank you so much for your interest and support in [i]Quality Dreams, Reasonably Priced[/i]. It means the world to us and it helps us out immensely! 💛[/p][p] [/p][p]If you haven’t wishlisted the full game yet, please please do so. (And please bother other people you know to wishlist it haha) We live and die at the whim of the Steam algorithm, and she is fed with wishlists.[/p][p] [/p][p]Also, if you liked this style of update, please let us know! We can do more of these for other characters if so :)[/p][p] [/p]

notes.title: behind the scenes: Jin's story
notes.content:
Greetings psychlines!

This week, we’ve got something special from behind the scenes to share with you: a flash fic we wrote when we first started solidifying Jin’s character. It’s set about two weeks before the game starts.

We thought it might be fun to see where the character started and how their voice has changed. The story also gives a sneak peek at some details from Jin’s life that aren’t in the demo as well as some more of what’s going on in their head.

Enjoy and let us know what you think! 💛
And if you want more behind the scenes content, follow us on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3164710/Quality_Dreams_Reasonably_Priced/]Steam[/url] or [url=https://linktr.ee/zorkiestudios]social media[/url], or join our newsletter on [url=https://substack.com/@zorkiestudios]Substack[/url].

____

I started my new job last week and it’s… Well, it’s fine. It pays the bills and that’s the important part. And sometimes it can be nice. When I look past all the selling and upselling and cross-selling, and just focus on the people. It’s been nice to learn about clients and be in a position to offer helping advice. 

For example, this older lady came in with her grandkid to get matching nanobot-animated tattoos. That was so sweet! They were happy and it was harmless and fun. (And I got paid a ton for bringing in two customers.)

Right, trying to focus on the human aspect. 

It’s hard to ignore the money. Especially when I’m barely scraping by. I’m hardly doing better than paycheck-to-paycheck at this point. I’ve been pushed out of the apartment I can no longer afford into one a few floors down that I can barely afford. It’s hard not to think about money when my budget passed tight a month ago and is well on its way to suffocating.

I’ve thought about giving up Nibbles to a friend. I’ve thought about it a lot. But I’m worried that faced with this wall of problems on my own, I’ll never make it to the other side. I need a bit of love, compassion, and companionship, and Nibbles has always been there for me. Giving her up would be worse than deprival, it would be tearing out a piece of my heart.

I’m trying to stay positive. Really, I swear. Things are slowly starting to look better, especially with this new job. It pays better, the hours aren’t bad, and my boss is only 70% the worst. I get to talk to people, get to know them. In not too long, I’ll hopefully have saved enough to move someplace better. 

I’m trying to fill myself with hope and tie it into a raft to carry me onwards. Maybe it won’t be today or tomorrow, but one day soon, I think I’ll wake up and know deep in my heart that things will get better. That they are getting better. That I am pulling myself back together one day at a time.

notes.title: only a few days until demo release 🌟
notes.content:
Hello body mod salespeople! 

As we wrap up the final touches on our demo, I want to take a moment to chat about the client interviews in [i]Quality Dreams, Reasonably Priced[/i].

These sessions really make up the heart of the game. They hold key moments where we ask you to learn about someone else and empathize with them, before then deciding whether to put their wellbeing ahead of your character’s.

For some clients, the decision is easy; for some, you might start thinking of them one way and end a different way; and some lie in a moral grey zone, where just your understanding and biases are left to support your decision. 

Since these scenes are so critical to conveying the themes and emotions of the game, we put a lot of thought into how they’re crafted. Each client interview has a uniquely designed dialogue flow based on the client’s personality and how they converse. Jin (the player character)’s job is to understand others and communicate with them, so we shape dialogue options based on how Jin understands the client’s conversation norms. The client then responds to these options based on their own feelings and understanding of the situation.

Take Ocean, the first client you meet in the game, as an example. (And mild spoiler warning here for anyone wanting to go into the game completely blind.)

Ocean is fairly straightforward, but he feels bit uneasy sharing about some topics. They’re also often willing to give the benefit of the doubt, choosing to be cordial and open until someone proves him wrong. Because of this, Jin will slowly breach and issue, generally only diving in more if Ocean seems open to talking about it. 

On Ocean’s side, the game tracks how many times you’ve upset him or said something that they view as a red flag. This is the main thing that impacts Ocean’s willingness to share—he starts out giving you a baseline of trust and then watches to see if you abuse it. This, and Ocean’s straightforward honesty, makes them one of the easier characters to talk to in the game.

We hope you enjoy meeting and chatting with Ocean in our demo (coming out in the next few days!). Be sure to let us know what you think of them and of the rest of the demo 💛

notes.title: upcoming demo 🎉
notes.content:
Greetings sellers of all things body mod!

We’ve got some very exciting updates for the new year 🌟

First and foremost, we’re preparing to release[b] a demo of [i]Quality Dreams, Reasonably Priced[/i] (QDRP)[/b] to Steam in the upcoming months.

The reason for our demo launch is tied to our second exciting news item: [i]QDRP[/i] will be participating in two upcoming festivals! Namely, [b]The Storyteller’s Festival[/b] and the [b]Women’s Day Game Showcase[/b]. 

We’ll be dropping a demo to coincide with the festivals and will be extra active on our socials, so feel free to reach out to us there or by email! We’d love to hear your feedback on the demo 💛


Those of you wanting to go into the demo 100% blind stop reading here! I’ll be going over some of its details next.



In the demo, you’ll meet Jin, the protagonist. You’ll get to experience some key scenes from the first three days of the game. These include meeting with and consulting two clients, having a performance review with your boss, and spending some quality time at home with your rabbit! 

While upselling functionality isn’t ready to share yet, we will have a bit of budgeting available! The budgeting features will be basic, but they should give you a sense of what it’ll be like in the full game. 

The demo will include five characters (including Jin), one adorable rabbit, four backgrounds, just under 30k words, and just over 1000 choice options. Each scene has multiple endings, and decisions made in each scene will be felt throughout the game. Your relationships with characters are tracked separately, and in the full game, they can influence each other’s opinions of you.


Hopefully you’re as excited to try the demo as we are to share it with you! Stay tuned for future updates 💛
